$comment: Budget for the boot payload: the entry chunk plus its static-import
closure. That is the JavaScript a phone must download, parse and compile
before the app renders anything, so it is the number that decides how
slow Patcher feels on mobile.
Chunks behind a dynamic import are deliberately not counted. Moving code
behind React.lazy or import() is the fix this budget exists to encourage.
maxBootBytes / maxBootBrotliBytes are a ratchet set 3% above the measured
payload: enough for a normal feature's worth of shell code and for build
noise, tight enough that a barrel regression cannot hide inside it. Lower
them when a change wins headroom. Raising one is a deliberate decision
that needs a reason in the pull request, not a routine edit.
RAISED TWICE. The first time the reason was not a feature: the Patcher
rename found this check failing by 104 KB raw / 28 KB brotli, and main
failed it identically, because no CI run had ever executed on main (the
job runs for pull requests only). Those values recorded the payload that
actually shipped.
The second time, on #147, the 3% headroom set then had been spent by
features — 1771 KB to 1824.6 KB raw across the work since — and a launch
dialog went over by 0.1 KB. Checked before raising: moving that dialog
behind React.lazy cut 1.1 KB raw but added 2.7 KB brotli, because the
split moved shared dialog code into chunks that compress worse. Both
values were reset to 3% above the payload measured then (1868394 raw /
487769 brotli bytes).
What the first note blamed is not the cause, measured on #147: it said
@hugeicons/core-free-icons does not tree-shake and put the whole free set
in the boot payload. It does tree-shake — the boot chunk carries 135 icon
element arrays against the 134 icons shared-ui's icon.tsx imports plus its
two inlined ones, about 100 KB, which is what those icons weigh. Per-icon
imports would win nothing.
There is deliberately no per-chunk limit. Parse and compile cost scales
with the total bytes on the boot path, not with how they are divided, so
splitting one boot chunk into two would satisfy a per-chunk cap while
making the page slightly slower for the extra request.
forbiddenBootPackages is the more important half. These packages are all
large and all needed only after a user action (open a diff, focus the
composer, render math). Each one reached the boot path through a barrel
re-export rather than a direct import, which type checking cannot catch,
so the check names them explicitly.
